original_finding_title: Assertions must not exceed evidence strength
source_claim_scope: Financial projections with explicit assumptions and risk wording show domain-specific evidence qualifiers, not a measured scriptwriting result.

original_finding_title: Cognitive load — teach one chunk at a time, worked examples before practice
source_claim_scope: Official CFPB page pairs a topical short video with a related teaching tool; not empirical support for a mandated cognitive-load chunk size.

source_claim_scope: MOOC viewing sessions correlate with length and production style; not randomized content chunking or comprehension.

original_finding_title: Modality effect — narrate visuals, don't caption them
source_claim_scope: Comparisons of production styles with speech and image, not a test that narrating visuals is always best.

original_finding_title: Never present unverified knowledge as verified
source_claim_scope: The dated BBC editorial note explicitly forbids misleading wildlife footage and commentary.

original_finding_title: No fabricated dialogue, composite characters, or misleading compression
source_claim_scope: BBC 2012 permits disclosed truthful compression/composite life-cycle representation in some cases; blanket prohibition on all composite representation is too broad.

original_finding_title: Assertions must not exceed evidence strength
source_claim_scope: Voiceover must not assert a named animal or location not truthfully depicted; original registered page inaccessible, dated BBC PDF is evidence.

original_finding_title: Avoid idioms, culture-specific references, and modifier stacks for international audiences
source_claim_scope: Interlingual subtitle translation and accessibility captions serve different intended audiences; no empirical translation-efficacy claim.

original_finding_title: Modality effect — narrate visuals, don't caption them
source_claim_scope: Synchronized speech/non-speech captions are needed for people who cannot hear; not evidence about narrator-visual alignment caused retention.

original_finding_title: Redundancy effect — don't narrate on-screen text
source_claim_scope: Any universal avoidance of concurrent on-screen and spoken words ignores accessibility requirements; W3C is normative not a viewer-performance test.
